messages.subject: legend in R/qtlChart
parts:
Hi Everyone!

I'm using the R/qtlChart to draw the figures for my QTL results. I have two questions:

(1) Is it possible to draw the legend for the heat map while we are using function 'iplotMScanone'? I have check the ChartOpt, but I didn't find any setting about the legend.

(2) Is it possible to to make the heat map only show colour on the loci that have the LOD above the permutation threshold? I thought it should also be in the setting, right? But o DIDN'T MANAGE.

(3) I want to add a title to the plot made by 'iplotMScanone'. I tried to add 'caption' in the setting for this command, but it gave me error. Do you know any way to do this?

Thanks a lot!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: legend in R/qtlChart
parts: (1) Is it possible to draw the legend for the heat map while we are using function 'iplotMScanone'? I have check the ChartOpt, but I didn't find any setting about the legend.
There's no option to include a legend.
(2) Is it possible to to make the heat map only show colour on the loci that have the LOD above the permutation threshold? I thought it should also be in the setting, right? But o DIDN'T MANAGE.

There's a chart option zthresh. Use it like this:

library(qtl)
library(qtlcharts)
data(grav)
grav <- calc.genoprob(grav, step=1)
grav <- reduce2grid(grav)
phecol <- seq(1, nphe(grav), by=5)
times <- attr(grav, "time")[phecol]
out <- scanone(grav, phe=phecol, method="hk")

iplotMScanone(out, times=times, chartOpts=list(zthresh=3))
(3) I want to add a title to the plot made by 'iplotMScanone'. I tried to add 'caption' in the setting for this command, but it gave me error. Do you know any way to do this?

The caption will give text below the chart.

iplotMScanone(out, times=times, chartOpts=list(zthresh=3,
                                        caption="This is a caption"))

But unfortunately it seems I failed to implement a chart title for iplotMScanone(). Sorry.

karl

parts:
Yes, that's right. But the interpolation of colors, between slateblue
and white, and between white and crimson, are done in javascript. So it
may be trick to ensure that your scales are exactly right. Personally, I
feel like color scales are not too useful to me and prefer the ability
to hover over different areas and have the tool tips indicate the
corresponding values.

karl
